sourcedFrom: Primary Weapons Systems BDE762-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE762-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") (ABSENT — no copyright line or date printed; the edition string V26.1 is the only revision mark)
cleanIntro:
The BDE762-TI is a modular .30-caliber can printed in titanium: a 3D-printed entrance chamber, a 3D-printed main baffle stack, four CNC-turned modular baffles, a flat end cap, and a removable 5/8-24 direct-thread mount on the chamber's 1.375-24 (HUB) threads. Every joint is a threaded joint, and every one comes apart with the two wrenches that ship with it.

PWS rates it up to .300 Win Mag on a barrel of at least 20 inches, and puts the interval at every 500 rounds: clean, lubricate, and check torque. The short K version (BDE762K-TI) is the same can without the modular baffles; this guide is the full-length one.

steps.title: Host treated as loaded until you have proved it empty
steps.action: Before the can is touched, the host it is on gets cleared by that firearm's own procedure: magazine out, action open, chamber looked into and seen empty. A suppressor coming off a barrel puts your hands at the muzzle, so the host is empty first.
steps.quote: TREAT ALL FIREARMS AS LOADED AT ALL TIMES.
steps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE762-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE762-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — WARNINGS, rule 2, printed p.6

steps.title: Let it cool completely before it comes off
steps.action: Wait until the can is cold to the touch before you reach for it. A titanium can stays hot well after the barrel feels fine, and PWS says it runs far hotter than the point where skin burns. Set it down touching nothing while it cools.
steps.caution: Do not handle a hot suppressor.
steps.quote: Allow the firearm and suppressor to completely cool prior to any contact.
steps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE762-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE762-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — WARNINGS, SUPPRESSORS GET HOT, printed p.4

steps.title: Gloves, goggles, and air
steps.action: Put on gloves and eye protection before the can opens. The fouling inside a can is toxic, and PWS ties its warranty to taking these precautions. Work somewhere ventilated and nowhere near a flame, because solvent comes next.
steps.aside: You should clean your suppressor in a wellventilated area away from open flame.
steps.quote: When cleaning a suppressor, you should wear gloves and safety goggles.
steps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE762-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE762-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — WARNINGS, CLEANING, printed p.4

steps.title: Two supplied wrenches, parts diagram open
steps.action: Use the two wrenches that came with the can. They work against each other, so one holds while the other turns. Keep the parts diagram (printed p.7) in front of you, because the order the parts come off is the order they go back.
steps.aside: Please review the parts diagram refererenced earlier in the manual when disassembling.
steps.quote: simply use the 2 supplied wrenches to seperate each part of the assembly.
steps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE762-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE762-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — MODIFICATIONS, printed p.11

steps.title: Seat the wrench notch before you turn
steps.action: The large side of each wrench carries a small notch that has to sit against the outside of the can. A wrench that is only half on slips under load and scores the DLC finish. A thin cloth between wrench and can protects the finish further.
steps.caution: Ensure that the wrench is securely aligned to avoid scratches to the surface finish.
steps.aside: You can use a thin cloth between the wrench and suppressor to better protect the finish.
steps.quote: The large side of the wrench has a small notch which aligns to the exterior of the suppressor.
steps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE762-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE762-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — MODIFICATIONS, printed p.11

steps.title: End cap and modular baffles off the main stack
steps.action: Turn off the flat end cap, then up to four modular baffles, each one off the main baffle stack. The wrench diagram marks which end does this job. Lay each part down in the order it came off.
steps.aside: The supplied wrenches can be used in opposite directions to make disassembly and reassembly easier.
steps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE762-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE762-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — MODIFICATIONS, wrench diagram, printed p.11

steps.title: Thread mount off the entrance chamber
steps.action: The 5/8-24 thread mount unthreads from the entrance chamber. This is the tightest joint on the can, torqued higher than the rest, so expect it to take more force to break loose. With it off, the entrance chamber's own 1.375-24 threads show, and those threads take a HUB mount.
steps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE762-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE762-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — MODIFICATIONS, wrench diagram, printed p.11

steps.title: Nylon brush and CLP, a soak for stuck carbon
steps.action: Brush each part with a nylon brush and a CLP-type product. Use nylon only on this can. Any part with carbon that will not brush off goes into a CLP soak and gets brushed again afterward.
steps.aside: You can soak individual parts in CLP for any stuck-on carbon.
steps.quote: To clean any part of this assembly, use a nylon brush with CLP (Cleaner, Lubricant, Preservative) type of product.
steps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE762-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE762-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — MAINTENANCE, printed p.14

steps.title: Look through the bore path
steps.action: Hold each part up to the light and look down the bore. Mud, sand or anything else lodged in the path is an obstruction. A bullet will strike it, so it comes out before the can goes back on a barrel.
steps.quote: Visually inspect the suppressor for any bore obstructions including natural matter like mud and/or sand.
steps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE762-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE762-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — MAINTENANCE, printed p.14

steps.title: Mind what touches the outside
steps.action: The outside of the can is DLC-coated. PWS warns that some cleaners and solvents should not be used on it, but the book does not say which. CLP is the product it names, so use CLP on the outside and nothing harsher.
steps.quote: Please be aware that the exterior is DLC (Diamond-like carbon) coated, so certain cleaners and solvents should not be used.
steps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE762-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE762-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — MAINTENANCE, printed p.14

steps.title: Oil or grease on every thread going back
steps.action: Before any joint goes back together, put a film of oil or grease on its threads. Carbon that bakes into dry threads can lock two parts together.
steps.quote: When reassembling/installing your suppressor, we suggest applying oil or grease on the threads to avoid carbon locking between parts.
steps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE762-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE762-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — MAINTENANCE, printed p.14

deepAbsentReason: There is nothing below this. PWS publishes one procedure for the BDE762-TI, the one above: separate each threaded part with the two supplied wrenches (printed p.11), brush and soak in CLP (printed p.14), and reassemble to torque (printed pp.11-12). The parts diagram (printed p.7) shows the 3D-printed entrance chamber and the 3D-printed baffle stack each as a single part, and the book's safety list forbids changing the can's internal components (printed p.6), so no deeper teardown exists in it to quote.

cleaning.name: BAFFLES AND END CAP
tasks: Main baffle stack, each modular baffle and the end cap brushed with nylon and CLP
Stuck-on carbon soaked in CLP, then brushed again
Parts laid out in the order they came off

cleaning.name: ENTRANCE CHAMBER AND MOUNT
tasks: Entrance chamber and thread mount brushed with nylon and CLP
Bore path checked clear of mud, sand or anything else lodged in it
Do not alter or change the can's internal components

cleaning.name: DLC EXTERIOR
tasks: Outside wiped with CLP, nothing harsher
Wrench notch seated and a thin cloth under it, so the finish is not scratched

cleaning.name: THREADS
tasks: Oil or grease on every thread before it goes back together
⛔ Never thread a modular baffle or the end cap straight onto the entrance chamber: the thread pitch is different and it damages the threads

cleaning.name: ⛔ THE SCHEDULE IS THE MAINTENANCE
tasks: Every 500 rounds: clean, lubricate and check torque

⚠ The book gives two torque figures: 25 ft. lbs. for all parts and 30 ft. lbs. for the mount to the entrance chamber on its torque page, and 7 ft. lb. in its maintenance warning. Ask PWS which one applies before you tighten to the lower figure
Fit and retention on the host checked before each use

reassembly: Every thread gets a film of oil or grease before it is started.

The main baffle stack threads onto the entrance chamber. The modular baffles go onto the stack, any or all four for the length you want, and the end cap goes on last. ⛔ Never thread a modular baffle or the end cap straight onto the entrance chamber: its thread pitch is different.
Torque with a 3/8" torque wrench on the supplied wrench: all parts to 25 ft. lbs., the thread mount to the entrance chamber to 30 ft. lbs. Do not go past the spec. Overtightening damages the can.
With the end cap straight on the main stack (no modular baffles), the can is at its shortest. PWS tested its hearing-safe rating in that configuration with factory ammunition.
Thread it onto a 5/8-24 barrel rated for it: up to .300 Win Mag, with a barrel of at least 20 inches.
fncheck: Off the gun: every joint is snug and nothing rattles when you shake the can. Look through the bore path from both ends and see light all the way through. On the host, before each use: the mount is fully threaded onto the barrel and every part is tight. PWS puts this check on the owner before every use. If the can is worn, loose, or does not fit the host properly, stop using it.
